subject: physics
question_text: Write the expression for the variation of pressure with depth in a fluid.

mark_split.label: P = P₀ + hρg, name every symbol
hρg alone is the gauge pressure

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 10 Very Short Answer Question 3 (printed p.105). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The book's own printed answer gives only P = hρg for this expression, which is the gauge pressure, the pressure due to the liquid column alone — it omits the surface term P₀ entirely. The full and correct expression is P = P₀ + hρg, and that is what this card writes; the 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: at depth h in a fluid at rest, P = P₀ + hρg, where P₀ is the pressure at the free surface; hρg alone is the gauge pressure, the excess of the pressure at depth h over the surface pressure.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: P = P₀ + hρg, name every symbol
lines: At a depth h below the surface of
a fluid at rest, the pressure is
where P₀ is the pressure at the
surface, ρ is the density of the
fluid and g is the acceleration
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write P = P₀ + hρg and name every symbol: P₀ the surface pressure, ρ the density, g the acceleration due to gravity.
steps.why: Pressure grows with depth because each added layer of fluid adds its own weight on top of what the surface already carries, so the surface term P₀ has to appear in the expression, not just the added part.
common_mistakes: Writing only P = hρg and leaving out P₀, which drops the pressure already present at the surface.
Taking h along a slanted path instead of the vertical depth.

recall.must_convey: That the pressure at depth h is P equals P naught plus h rho g, with P naught the pressure at the surface, rho the density and g the acceleration due to gravity.
accept: P naught plus h rho g
surface pressure plus h rho g
P equals P naught plus h rho g
reject: h rho g alone is the gauge pressure

steps.memory_tip: Depth adds on top of the surface: P = P₀ + hρg, never hρg alone.

steps.label: hρg alone is the gauge pressure
lines: The term hρg by itself is called
the gauge pressure: the amount by
which the pressure at depth h
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Name hρg on its own as the gauge pressure, the excess over the surface pressure.
steps.why: Separating the excess term from the surface term is what makes P₀ + hρg more than a formula to memorise — it explains why a gauge reads zero at the surface and rises with depth.
common_mistakes: Calling the whole sum P = P₀ + hρg the gauge pressure. Only the hρg part is.
Confusing hρg with the absolute pressure, which is P₀ + hρg together.

recall.must_convey: That hρg on its own, without P naught, is called the gauge pressure — the excess of the pressure at depth h over the surface pressure.
accept: the excess over the surface pressure
gauge pressure is the added term
reject: P equals P naught plus h rho g

steps.memory_tip: hρg alone is the gauge reading; add P₀ to get the absolute pressure.

insider_note: Two marks: the full expression P = P₀ + hρg with every symbol named, then that hρg alone, without P₀, is the gauge pressure. Writing only hρg for the expression leaves out the surface term.
